title: Adaptive stage latency economizer and fairness allocator (entropy-probed kernel steering)
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: tail latency spikes and unfair tenant slowdowns when the runtime makes static kernel selection decisions for prefill/decode. Existing allocators either prioritize throughput (aggressive coalescing) or prioritize strict latency SLOs (single-tenant hedging). We need a middle-ground that dynamically trades throughput for latency based on short-term entropy signals and kernel probe cost estimates, while preventing starvation across tenants.
design_notes: High-level: introduce an adaptive Stage Latency Economizer (SLE) that: 1) continuously probes a small sample of kernels (kernel-probing) to update a per-model, per-seqlen latency and memory profile; 2) computes an entropy-derived admission signal for each incoming request window indicating how much batching/merge risk exists; 3) uses a fairness allocator that applies an exponential leaky-bucket per-tenant to guarantee progress while allowing opportunistic coalescing when entropy is low.
proposed_solution_list: Kernel Probe Agent: lightweight microbenchmarks run on a subset of warm workers to estimate tail effects of kernel paths (int4, fused-attn, split-attn). Results fed into a small in-memory table keyed by (model, seqlen_bucket, kernel_family).
Entropy Window: measure token distribution / request divergence across a sliding 200ms window. High entropy -> avoid merging prefills; low entropy -> allow larger consolidations.

Stage Latency Economizer (SLE): uses probe table + entropy to compute a latency budget and an aggressiveness score. Aggressiveness controls prefill splitting: how many micro-phases to emit, how aggressively to merge decode microbatches, and whether to route to lower-cost kernels that increase variance.
Fairness Allocator: per-tenant exponential leaky-bucket with a tunable debt cap to avoid starvation. When debt approaches cap, the SLE reduces aggressiveness for that tenant until debt decays.
Hedging Hooks: optional speculative hedges for requests that exceed a latency budget, launching a thin-path single-tenant kernel in parallel when queue time > threshold.
Observability: new SLE metrics (aggressiveness, entropy_score, kernel_probe_version), tenant debt, and an SLO breach attribution linkable to a request trace.
Fallback Policy: when probe data is stale (>10s) or entropy signals are noisy, default to conservative latency-first split with smaller merges.
experiment_plan_list: Stage A (canary): run SLE in simulation mode for 48h on ~1% of traffic for model family xglm-4/8k. Collect metrics but do not change allocations.
Stage B (shadow): enable SLE decisions but only apply them to <10% of workers in dedicated pool; compare tail latency and tokens/sec against control using deterministic sampling.
Stage C (ramp): progressively enable SLE for 25% -> 50% -> 100% in a burst-tolerant region if P95 latency improves or cost reduces without increasing P99 by >5%.
Duration & Rollback: each ramp step 72h observation window; automatic rollback on P99 degradation >8% or customer_impact high.
A/B instrumentation: add tags on requests to attribute to SLE path, capture kernel choice, prefill/merge counts, and tenant debt at request completion.
metrics: P50, P95, P99 latency (prefill and decode)
acceptance_criteria: Stable probe table with >90% probe_success_ratio for targeted kernels
No increase in customer-impacting P99 >5% across canary models
Throughput (tokens/sec) improves or cost_per_token reduces by >=6% for low-entropy workloads
Per-tenant starvation_count remains near zero; debt decays under configured cap within 30s after spike
Observability dashboards show clear attribution for SLE decisions and hedges
rollout_plan: Deploy Kernel Probe Agent to runtime rollout-canary image. Enable SLE flag gating. Start with Stage A simulation, review logs and dashboards, then Stage B shadow, then Stage C ramp with automated checks. Post-rollout, enable long-term metrics retention for SLE signals and schedule a postmortem evaluation after 2 weeks.
